newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates drop on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates drop on low demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates fell on Monday on low demand after the government slashed duties on imports of raw cotton and synthetic fibres as part of a relief package for the textile industry, dealers said.
"Prices are likely to slip further as current rates in the market are much higher than imported cotton," said one.
He said spinners had already booked 80,000 480-lb bales of cotton during the past few days. "Why should they pay 2,500 rupees for the quality they can import at 2,300 rupees," the dealer said.
The kerb rate for NIAB-78 variety was at 2,100 rupees ($52.21) per maund (37.32 kg) while MNH-93 was traded at 2,200 rupees, dealers said.
